training.inputs: The same 55 train-fit requests and two grouped long-training shards used by the qualifying CV; no other split may contribute fitting rows or statistics.
training.procedure: For every routed layer, fit one rank-32 head for the already-frozen eight epochs on every authorized training row, using the frozen int4 feature transform, causal history, request balancing, optimizer, seed, numeric mode, and resource limits.
training.model_output: Persist every final head tensor and training report with exact array schemas and SHA-256 bindings before opening the diagnostic archive.

diagnostic.input: Only the isolated train-precision-diagnostic shard containing the five cases excluded from fitting and rank selection.
diagnostic.pairing: On each retained FP16 holdout row that has a valid K-token target, score the identical frozen head twice. One arm uses the stored FP16 gate input and the other uses the frozen int4 reconstruction; causal-history features, targets, row order, and budgets are identical.
diagnostic.headline: K=4, budget=32, unweighted macro-request recall
secondary: all K/budget recall, precision, waste, and full-set coverage

acceptance.formula: deficit_pp = 100 * (FP16 metric - int4 metric); negative values are not clipped
acceptance.failure_action: Do not attribute later held-out failure to the probe concept and do not adopt the int4 feature online; report the paired result before deciding whether a new higher-precision corpus is worth collecting.

isolation.forbidden: Calibration and test archives remain unopened. Diagnostic results cannot change rank, optimizer, epochs, feature definition, or thresholds.
isolation.claim_limit: This measures feature-quantization sensitivity on five known diagnostic cases. It is not held-out probe performance and is not a serving-speed claim.
